$comment: The map: what this app is made of, and where you touch it to change each part.
Same rule as docs/validation/ledger.json — one source, several renderers. This file
is the only place the map is written; `make map` prints it, `make map FEATURE=<id>`
prints one feature, and the /extend skill drives a session from it. Never restate a
feature's entrypoints anywhere else; point at the id.
WHY THIS IS JSON AND NOT PROSE, and why it holds symbols instead of line numbers:
an orientation doc is only worth reading if it is true, and the usual ones rot
silently — a file gets renamed, a function moves, and the map keeps confidently
pointing at nothing. scripts/gate-map.mjs runs in CI and in the pre-commit hook: it
opens every file listed here and checks that every `symbol` still literally appears
in it. A rename fails the build on the commit that does the renaming, naming the map
entry to update. Line numbers are what rots fastest, so they are never stored — the
renderer computes them at print time, so what you read is always where it is now.
FIELDS
id         kebab-case, stable; what you pass to `make map FEATURE=`.
what       one line, in the user's terms, not the code's.
layer      L1 core | L2 web | L3 etl | gate — where this feature's weight sits.
entry      the ordered path through the code. Read them top to bottom and you have
the feature. `file` + `symbol` (checked) + `note` (why you'd stop here).
extend     ordered steps for the most common change to this feature. Written as
what to do, not what exists.
gates      what will judge the change — run these before you believe it works.
seeAlso    ids of features that will notice if you change this one.
ADDING A FEATURE: add an entry here. The gate does not require one per file, and it
should not — a map that lists everything is an `ls`. List what someone arriving
cold would otherwise have to find by grep.

features.what: Tap an ayah on the page, or drag a marquee across several, and see amber marker swipes laid over them.

entry.note: The one decision the whole surface rests on: is this pointer a pan, a pinch, a tap, or a marquee? Everything downstream is a consequence. TAP_SLOP_PX and LONG_PRESS_MS are the thresholds a finger is judged by.
Screen point → ayah key, via the polygon manifest. The adapter between geometry and scripture; nothing above this layer knows what a polygon is.

Owns #hifth-overlay and every mark drawn in it. Framework-free and imperative on purpose — React must not re-render the stage. If you are adding a new kind of highlight, it is a StyleToken here, not a component. `paint` is where a style becomes either marker swipes or a cloned shape.

Why the highlight looks like a pen and not a box. Every ayah's hit area is a run of axis-aligned rectangles, one per line it occupies; this turns each into a band along the line's middle. It is a parser with a fallback, not an assumption — it returns null on any geometry it does not fully recognise and the Highlighter clones the shape instead, so an unfamiliar page from Loop 4b degrades to the old box rather than to nothing.
The React boundary. Binds @use-gesture to the surface, hands events to pointerIntent, and calls the Highlighter imperatively. The only file where the two worlds touch.

extend: Add the intent to `PointerIntent` and teach `pointerIntent`/`nextIntent` when to return it — with a unit test in gestures.test.ts first, because this is pure and cheap to pin.

If it draws something new, add a `StyleToken` and its branch in the Highlighter, then a CSS custom property in apps/web/src/styles/tokens.css. Decide whether it is ink: if so add it to `INKED` and give it an `--ink-*` token, because the ink rules blend with `multiply` and the alpha washes are tuned for compositing over — the two families are not interchangeable.
Wire it in PageStage. Resist adding state to React that the Highlighter already owns.
Add a golden row if it changes pixels — see the `golden-images` feature.

features.what: From a selected ayah, jump to the mutashabihat that resemble it — the reason this app exists.

entry.note: Loads and caches the per-surah edge shards from public/assets/adj/. Start here to understand what an edge IS.
Edges → rail chips, grouped by direction. `orderForHifz` beside it is the ranking a memoriser actually wants, which is not the ranking the data arrives in.
The chips down the side. Arabic-Indic digits throughout, including in aria-labels — a sighted reader seeing ٣ and a screen-reader user hearing 'three' is a defect, and one the aria snapshots caught.
The chip's expansion: the destinations, and the diff against the current ayah.

The cross-page jump itself, and the case that is easy to get wrong: the destination is on another page, so the page must mount before the wash can land. `navigatedRef` is what stops an in-flight fetch from stomping a deep link that already arrived.
Where you have been. The hop is only useful if you can get back.

extend: New edge kind: add it to `EDGE_TYPES` in adjacency.ts and give it a status. `isActiveEdgeType` is what keeps a provisional kind out of the UI while its data is still being audited.
Emit it from packages/etl/scripts/build-adjacency.mjs, then re-run `make etl` — CI diffs the committed shards against a fresh ETL run, so a non-deterministic change fails the build.
If a human has ruled on specific edges, they belong in the curated set, not the dataset — gate:verified-edges enforces that a 'correct' edge still ships and a 'wrong' one stays gone, forever.
Check the shard budget in the ETL output; the largest shard is printed on every run.

features.what: Show every ayah sharing an Arabic root with this one — the other way ayahs rhyme.

entry.note: Two shard families: per-ayah refs and per-root buckets. The split is what keeps a 44k-pair index inside the byte budget on a phone.
Ranking for someone holding a mushaf: near pages first, because that is how the memory is organised.
The ⬡ surface. Note the glyph is shared with a rail chip and the two promise different things — that collision was a decided defect, not an accident.

extend: Roots are derived, never hand-edited: change packages/etl/scripts/build-roots.mjs and re-run `make etl`.
Granularity is ayah-level today. Word-level is the open design (see the roadmap) and would change RootOccurrence, not just the UI.

features.what: Every view has a URL, and every URL restores its view — offline, from a cold start.

entry.note: State → hash. Its inverse `parseHash` must round-trip it; that pair is the whole contract and it is unit-tested as a pair.
Hash → state, and the place to be forgiving: a hand-typed or truncated link should degrade to something sensible rather than a blank page.
The React binding. Hash routing, not history routing, because this ships as static files with no server to rewrite paths.
Where a link leaves the app. Do not reach for the Clipboard API without a fallback — a LAN preview is plain http, so it is not a secure context and the API is simply absent.

extend: Add the field to `AppState`, then to both serializeState and parseHash in the same commit — a round-trip test is the cheapest way to keep them honest.
Old links must keep working. Treat the hash format as a published API, because it is: it is in people's notes and messages.
Add an e2e that opens the URL cold, rather than one that clicks its way to the state — those test different things and only the first tests a link.

features.what: Getting to a known place: the surah/ayah jumper, the keyboard map, and the coach marks that teach the gestures once.

entry.note: Parses what someone actually types — Arabic or Western digits, Arabic names with or without alif-lam, '2:255', 'p19'. `normalizeArabic` is the reason it tolerates real input.
The combobox, opened from the one glyph in the header that is not a mode. The row it lives in has 17 px of slack on a 320 px phone — see chrome-fit before adding anything to it.

The header fits every phone from 320 to 430, and is the same height at all of them. The second half is the one that bites: the stage gets what the chrome leaves, and the golden baselines are shots of the stage.
One pure function from (key, context) to action, so the keyboard map is testable without a DOM and cannot disagree with itself across components.
Shown once, keyed in localStorage. Every e2e that is not about coach marks must suppress them in an init script, or it is testing the coach marks.

extend: New input syntax: extend parseJump and its unit tests. Keep the UI dumb — it should render JumpTargets, not know how they were found.
New shortcut: add it to appKeyAction with a KeyContext branch, and add the row to the help surface in the same commit.
Anything added to the header row costs width the row does not have, and height the stage cannot spare. Run chrome-fit before and after, and if it needs a control, say which one it replaces.

features.what: Which mushaf print you are reading, and whether tajweed colouring is on.

entry.note: The registry. `EditionStatus` is what keeps an edition whose provenance is still PROVISIONAL out of the picker.
Maps an ayah between editions. Needed because ayah numbering is not universal and a share link must survive an edition switch.
Per-surah mark shards → per-ayah marks. `TAJWEED_RULES` is the rule vocabulary and the palette keys derive from it.
The switch. Skin swap must not re-render the stage — it changes classes on existing nodes.

extend: A new edition is a data change first: assets, a SOURCES.md entry with its licence, and a concordance. Only then a registry entry.
gate:license and gate:text-sources both read SOURCES.md — an edition whose provenance is not recorded cannot ship, by construction.
A new tajweed rule: add to TAJWEED_RULES, emit from build-tajweed.mjs, add the palette entry. The class prefix is centralised so CSS and TS cannot drift.

features.what: Works with the phone in aeroplane mode, a week after you last opened it.

entry.note: Registration and update flow. Service workers need a secure context — that is why offline specs cannot pass against a plain-http LAN or container URL, and it is the harness, not the app.

Eviction takes the precache and leaves the registration, so the worker never installs again and offline dies silently while every online signal still says healthy. The repair re-registers the same sw.js under a query-suffixed URL, because only a script the registration has never seen produces an install — measured, not assumed: reloads, update(), and unregister()+register() all leave the precache empty or resurrect the old worker. It waits for that install to finish, not for index.html to reappear: the shell is the first entry written and the app's scripts are the last.
Asks the browser not to evict us. It can say no, and the honest UI for that is a notice, not silence.
What the user is told about their storage — and the only place the install prompt is offered. Must not stack with the coach strip; must not move into the header, which has no width for it.

extend: Precache list and strategies live in the vite-plugin-pwa config in apps/web/vite.config.ts, not in a hand-written sw.js.
Adding to the precache costs install-time bytes on a phone. Check the entry count and size the build prints.
Test offline behaviour in an e2e that actually goes offline, over a secure context. A unit test cannot see a service worker.

Eviction is a separate case from offline and has its own describe in apps/web/e2e/offline.spec.ts: CDP Storage.clearDataForOrigin with storageTypes 'cache_storage' takes the caches and leaves the worker registered, which is the state a real ITP sweep leaves behind.
Anything that can fail to load a page must say so — see PageStage's error banner. A silent failure leaves the previous page on the stage while the chrome has already announced the new number.

features.what: The mushaf SVG pages themselves, and the polygon metadata that makes them clickable.

entry.note: Source SVG → the page asset plus its polygon manifest. Deterministic by requirement: CI re-runs it and fails on any byte of difference.
Fetch and cache a page in the browser. The one place that knows the asset URL shape.
Does the corpus actually cover what we claim? Coverage assumed rather than measured is how a missing page reaches a memoriser.

extend: Never hand-edit anything under apps/web/public/assets — it is generated, and the ETL determinism check in CI will reject it.
Change the producing script, run `make etl`, and commit the script and the regenerated output together.
gate:notext enforces that pages carry no <text> nodes: the glyphs are outlines, so rendering never depends on a font being installed.

features.what: Turning the mutashabihat dataset into the per-surah shards the app hops through.

entry.note: Dataset + curated edges → 114 shards. Reverse edges are generated here, so an edge stated once is navigable from both ends.
The 6236-ayah numbering the datasets speak, and its inverse. Every off-by-one bug in this project has lived within one function of this pair.

The +1 that bridges a 0-based dataset to a 1-based core. It shipped missing, and 47.8% of the hop corpus pointed at an ayah sharing no words with its source — a mutashabihat instrument being quietly, entirely wrong. Nothing caught it: the curated Loop-2 edges are written as "S:A" strings and skip this conversion, so every gate and every e2e stayed green over the only edges anyone had looked at. The comment above it carries the measurement; read it before touching numbering here.

The gate that would have caught the off-by-one on day one. Every dataset-derived edge is scored by the longest contiguous run of words its two ends share, and CI fails past 10% of them sharing none. Random ayah pairs score 69% there, the broken corpus scored 48%, the corrected one 3.9% — the threshold sits in a gap, not on a tuning knob.

The one reader of the vendored morphology, and the one definition of 'how similar are these two ayahs'. The gate enforces a floor on this number and the sampler prints it beside each pair a human audits — computed a second time, they would eventually disagree, and the human would be the one assumed wrong.

The spot-audit draw. Stratified by type × provenance × page distance, because 97% of the pairs are one class and a flat draw of twenty never shows the classes gate:edges cannot reach. The unit is the unordered pair, not the directed edge — the corpus generates both directions from one fact, so asking a reader about both spends the scarcest input this project has on a question already answered.

extend: Vendoring a new dataset: add the SOURCES.md entry with its licence in the same commit as the data. gate:license fails otherwise, deliberately.
Every script prints a summary line — counts in, counts out, largest shard. Read it; a silent 10% drop in edges looks exactly like success.
Human verdicts on specific edges are permanent. They go in the verified-edges register, and gate:verified-edges enforces them from then on.

Data here can be structurally perfect and semantically noise; gate:edges is the only check that reads meaning. A new edge type whose promise is shared phrasing belongs in its SCORED_TYPES, or it ships unmeasured.
A new edge type also becomes a new stratum in the spot-audit draw automatically, and `make validate` will show it as a class nobody has looked at until someone does.

features.what: Usable by someone who cannot see the page: labels on the polygons, a live region for what changed, and Arabic digits everywhere.

entry.note: Where an invisible polygon becomes a focusable, labelled control. If a new drawn thing should be reachable by screen reader or keyboard, it happens here.
One aria-live region for the whole app. Several would race and interrupt each other.
Every number a user hears or reads. The bug this prevents is a badge showing ٣ while the label says 'three' — invisible until an aria snapshot puts the two side by side.

The accessible tree, committed as text under e2e/__aria__/. Snapshots are text, not geometry, so they are keyed by project and not by platform — a Linux runner and a Mac must produce the same tree or one of them is wrong.

extend: Any new control: a label in Arabic, a 44px target, and a visible focus ring. The contrast spec checks the third and will fail you.
Numbers in user-facing strings go through toArabicDigits — including inside aria-labels, which is the half everyone forgets.
Update the aria snapshots deliberately (`--update-snapshots`) and read the diff. An accepted snapshot is the only place a broken tree can hide.

features.what: The visual gate: highlight geometry the DOM cannot describe, pinned as images.

entry.note: Golden images are keyed by {platform} because they are rasterized geometry. The aria snapshots beside them are keyed by {projectName} because they are text — mixing the two axes is a bug in both directions.

The pinned container. The generator and the checker must be the same rasterizer or the gate is a coin flip; gate:golden-env enforces that the Makefile, the CI job, and the installed Playwright all agree.
Why the baselines are committed to git rather than LFS, and the number at which that answer should be revisited.

extend: Adding a row means adding baselines for BOTH platforms: `make golden-update` for darwin, `make golden-linux UPDATE=1` for linux.
Open the changed PNGs before committing. An accepted baseline is the gate agreeing with you, which is worth nothing unless you looked.
Never bump Playwright without bumping GOLDEN_IMAGE and re-rendering — the failure mode is ten red diffs that look exactly like a UI regression.

features.what: The checks a machine cannot do — a phone in a hand, a mushaf on a table — tracked so they cannot quietly not happen.

entry.note: The only place a manual runbook is written. `make validate CHECK=<id>` prints it, `make guide` renders it for a phone, the /validate skill drives it.
Does NOT fail on outstanding checks — a phone that has not been held is a fact, not a broken build. It fails when the ledger lies.
Writes the verdict back and then prints what that verdict now obliges — the standing rule is that a manual result must tighten something automated.

The only writer of docs/validation/evidence/. Runs each check's declared `evidence.run` and writes the real exit code; everything else only reads. Exits 0 even when a producer goes red — a reporting run, not a gate.
Exit 3 is "could not tell", and it is not a pass — so a producer that could not reach its subject strikes no step off a human's runbook.
Derived from the check id, never stored beside it: a path written down in two places is a path that can disagree with itself.

extend: A new manual check is a ledger entry with a full runbook. A pending user-owned check with no steps fails the gate, because a check nobody can follow will not be run.
Edit the ledger and re-run `make guide` in the same commit — a staleness hash fails the build otherwise.
When a check comes back, record it and then do what `tunes` printed. That step is what turns a verdict into a permanent test instead of a note.

An `evidence` block must name a `residue` — say in words what the command cannot do. The gate rejects one that does not, because an automated run naming no remainder is one claiming to have done a human's job.

`evidence.covers` points at runbook step ids, never positions, and `evidence.run` is a script rather than a make target — make flattens every failed recipe to exit 2, which would let a network timeout read as a verdict.

features.what: Every glyph on screen traces to a named source under a named licence, and the offer to hand that source over resolves.

entry.note: The register of everything vendored. Not documentation — two gates parse it, so an entry is a load-bearing part of the build.
Fails if something is vendored without a recorded licence. The obligation is legal, so the check is mechanical.
What the user is actually told. Not authored here — each row is declared in its SOURCES.md ```colophon fence and this renders it, so the record and the screen cannot drift.
Enforces that binding, and refuses a non-commercial claim nobody recorded — the exact defect that once told every reader the KFGQPC artwork was more restricted than it is.
Where the offer points. It has to actually resolve for a stranger — that is a real obligation, not a nice-to-have.

The offer, followed the way a stranger would follow it: anonymously, no gh and no token, because signed in as ourselves a private repo looks public. Named `check-` and not `gate-` because it reaches the public internet and is deliberately not in `pnpm gates` — it runs on demand (`make source-offer`) and from the public-deploy workflow.

extend: Vendor nothing without its SOURCES.md entry in the same commit.
To change what the reader is told about a licence, edit that source's ```colophon fence in SOURCES.md. The component follows; gate:license-copy fails if it does not.
A source the app should not credit still has to say so — `not-credited: <reason>` in the fence. Silence is indistinguishable from an oversight, which is why it is not allowed.
A GPL-derived asset makes this repo the corresponding source. That constrains unrelated decisions, including whether binaries can live behind a metered service (see gate:golden-size).
Before publishing, run `make source-offer URL=<deployed>`. It is red today on purpose: the repository is private, so the offer 404s for everyone who is not us (task #53).

features.what: What judges a change, and the rule that every gate is reproducible locally.

entry.note: An exact mirror of the build-test-gate job, in CI order. If you add a step to one, add it to the other in the same commit — that promise is the whole value of the target.
Four jobs: secrets-scan, build-test-gate, e2e (containerised), lighthouse. Only the second is what `make ci` mirrors; the other three have their own make targets.
Every artifact CI uploads is one something actually produces. Written after an upload step preserved nothing for several loops while looking green.
This map, checked. Every symbol listed in docs/map.json must still exist, so the orientation doc cannot rot into confident fiction.

The promises, checked. docs/use-cases.json names the test behind each thing this app claims to do; this asserts those tests still exist and are still tests. Rename a test and the commit doing it is told which promise it was standing behind.

extend: A new gate is a script in scripts/, a `gate:*` entry in package.json, a line in `make ci`, and a step in build-test-gate. All four, or it does not run.
Verify a new gate by breaking the thing it protects and watching it fail, then reverting. A gate that has never failed has never been tested.
Gates fail with the fix in the message. 'X is wrong' costs someone an afternoon; 'X is wrong, run Y' costs them a minute.
